NFL.com shows the Colts at 3-7 and the Texans at 3-6, a small record gap for a 12.5-point spread, with key players out on both sides.
SportsLine's simulation model picks Over 44.5 and projects 51 total points; the page also says Texans WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and RB Woody Marks are out, while RB David Montgomery is set to return.
Covers' AI projects Texans 27-20, a 47-point total, and leans Over 44.5, but warns that Colts protection problems that stall drives would undercut the Over even if Houston controls the game.

Covers says Texans LB Azeez Al-Shaair, the leading tackler, went on IR; weather is a non-factor under the retractable roof; Kalshi prices shade slightly toward the Under at 44.5; and the analyst's pick is Colts +10.5, not the total.

findings.note: An Oct 28, 2026 report says Ekholm missed two games with an undisclosed injury and had only a goal and three points in 10 games. Its news feed also shows a later RotoWire item saying he would miss at least a week, so check his status for tonight.

The Oilers' own preview says Edmonton goes for a seventh straight win at Tampa and lists Ekholm among the NHL's plus-minus leaders. That suggests he is active and playing a big role, but the preview gives no specific lineup or injury confirmation.
Ekholm had 24 assists in 65 games in 2024-25, and his coach describes him as a top-pair, shutdown and penalty-kill defenseman with only part-time power-play work. That role limits his assist chances.
ESPN lists him as a Blue Jackets right wing with 2 goals and 8 assists in 18 games in 2026-27, but only 1 assist in 6 road games; this is a road game. The page's date is uncertain.
NHL.com's projected lineup for the Nov 17 game at the Islanders had him on the second line with Voronkov and Fantilli. I found no lineup or injury news for the Chicago game itself.

Covers shows he had assists in 3 of 6 games from Nov 3 to Nov 14, including Nov 14 against Philadelphia. Over 0.5 assists closed around +210 to +250 in those games, and the season average is 0.44 assists per game.

findings.note: Herro's ESPN page lists him as a Bucks guard with game-time-decision (GTD) status and a foot issue. It also shows a career average of 4.1 assists in 32.5 minutes, which is above the 3.5 line, though the exact date of the GTD tag isn't shown.

Herro's NBA.com profile says he is out with a foot injury for a Friday game against the Wizards. The note isn't clearly dated, so his availability for this Portland game is still uncertain and should be checked.

The Bucks traded Giannis Antetokounmpo to Miami for Herro and young players, so Herro moves into a post-Giannis Milwaukee team. That likely gives him a bigger on-ball creator role, which works against an assists Under.

Boozer is listed as Active and has started all 14 games at about 31 minutes. He shot 7-13 from three (29 points) at Washington on 11/16, but he made no threes against Toronto on 11/9 or Brooklyn on 11/14, so his recent 3PM swings widely. His season 3P% is 32.2.
In the first meeting with Golden State on Oct. 23, Boozer went 4-7 from three in 37 minutes, scoring 25 points with 13 rebounds. That is well over the 1.5 line against this opponent.

The Nov. 4 Rookie Ladder ranked Boozer No. 1 and listed him at 36.4% from three, including a 4-for-5 triple-double against Portland. It shows he is a featured, volume-shooting rookie, and I found no injury or role-reduction reports.

inputs.detail: Recency-weighted; the same figure the game-line model uses

inputs.label: His results vs. our forecasts
inputs.detail: 25 actual vs. 18.8 forecast points in earlier games; shrunk toward 1

steps.label: Opponent goals allowed vs. long-run league average
His results vs. our past forecasts

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 25 points against 18.8 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

blend.label: Production rate
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

blend.label: Ice time
blend.detail: Recency-weighted games; the rest is the position average

trend.label: assists
trend.note: Faded games count less. A game’s weight halves every 110 of his games for production and every 14 of his games for ice time.

missing: The starting goalie (team defense blends its goalies)

versus.note: History only, not a model input. In our backtests, results against one opponent did not predict the next meeting beyond a player’s overall form.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.

key_drivers: Projected ice time 19.0 minutes; separately shrunk production rate
uncertainties: Line and power-play assignment not verified
invalidation_conditions: New goalie, lineup or injury information
excluded.goalie_assumption: Projected, not confirmed. Opposing goalie, Buffalo Sabres: likely Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen 44% (sv 0.900), Colten Ellis 31%, Alex Lyon 25%.
excluded.lineup_assumption: Participation required for action; current role and active lineup unconfirmed

sensitivity.assumption: Production/opportunity means ±10%; not a confidence interval
